summary: One Time Secret lets you generate links for sensitive information that become invalid after a single access. It provides a straightforward method to transmit credentials or private notes without leaving a permanent record in communication histories.
goodFor: Systems administrators or developers who regularly need to share temporary passwords or API tokens securely with clients and colleagues.
watchOut: You must ensure that the recipient accesses the link before any unintended party intercepts it, as the system cannot verify the identity of the person who ultimately opens the secret.
deployNotes: As a containerised application built with Ruby and Node.js, you will typically run it via Docker alongside a persistent datastore like Redis or PostgreSQL. You will also need to configure a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
